title: Before the Ages, Sent, and Coming
english: …world, and that judgment will be given to Him.
95. That the sun and the moon will be darkened.
96. That the heavens will be rolled up.
97. That the Antichrist will come before the coming of Christ.
98. That he will kill many.
99. That then there will be a time of tribulation.
100. That Christ will come after him, and how He will come.
101. That the sign of Christ will be plain to see.
102. That the kingdom will have no end.
1. That the Son was begotten before the ages.
David the great is the first to say it, in Psalm 109: “From the womb, before the morning star, I begot You” (Psalm 110:3).

Wisdom, too, speaks in the same way: “Before the age He founded me, in the beginning, before He made the earth, and before He made the depths, and before the springs of the waters came forth, and before the mountains were settled; and before all the hills He begets me” (Proverbs 8:23-25).
And David says again, in Psalm 71: “He will endure with the sun, and before the moon, from generation to generation” (Psalm 72:5).
2. That He was with the Father.
Moses says, in the account of the creation of the world: “Let Us make man in Our image and after Our likeness” (Genesis 1:26).
3. That He is co-creator.

Wisdom says: “When He was preparing the heaven, I was present with Him; and when He was marking out His own throne; and when He was making the clouds above strong upon the winds; and when He was setting the springs beneath heaven firm; and when He was making the foundations of the earth strong, I was beside Him, fitting all things together” (Proverbs 8:27-30).
And David says in Psalm 32: “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the breath of His mouth all their host” (Psalm 33:6).
And again Wisdom says: “I saw Your works, being present when You were making the world” (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9).
4. That He was sent.

Isaiah speaks thus: “The Lord God, who made the heaven and fixed it, who made firm the earth and what is in it, who gives breath to the people upon it and breath to those who walk on it: I am the Lord God who called You, and I have given You as a covenant for the race, as a light for the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, to bring out from their chains those who are bound, and from the prison house those who sit in darkness” (Isaiah 42:5-7).
And Malachi says: “Behold, I send My messenger before Your face, and he will survey the way” (Malachi 3:1; Mark 1:2).
And again: “He has sent Me to bring good news to the poor” (Isaiah 61:1).
And David says in Psalm 106: “He sent His word and healed them” (Psalm 107:20).
5. That He will come.
Jacob says: “A ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until what is laid up comes; and He is the expectation of the nations” (Genesis 49:10).

Moses says: “The Lord God will raise up for you a Prophet from among his brothers, like me; you will listen to Him in all things. And whoever does not listen to that Prophet will be utterly destroyed for ever” (Deuteronomy 18:15, 19; Acts 3:22-23).
And Hosea says: “We will find Him ready as the dawn, and He will come to the earth like the early and the late rain” (Hosea 6:3).
And Amos says: “On that day He will raise up the fallen tent of David, and rebuild its ruins” (Amos 9:11).
Micah says: “On the tops of the mountains, out of Zion will go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem” (Micah 4:1-2).
And Joel says: “The Lord will cry out from Zion, and from Jerusalem He will utter His voice” (Joel 3:16).
And again: “You will know that He is the Lord our God, and that He will dwell on His holy mountain” (Joel 3:17).
And again: “The Lord will dwell in Zion” (Joel 3:21).
Obadiah says: “On Mount Zion there will be salvation; for the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations” (Obadiah 1:17, 15).
Jonah will be enough by himself to make plain the figure of the death (Jonah 1:17; Matthew 12:40).
And Nahum says: “The Lord is good to those who wait for Him.” “For behold, I am against you, says the Lord Almighty” (Nahum 1:7; 2:13).
And Habakkuk: “He will rise at the end, and at the appointed time; and if He is slow, wait for Him, for He will surely come and will not delay” (Habakkuk 2:3).
And again: “When the time has come, You will be shown forth” (Habakkuk 3:2).
And that “God will come from Teman” (Habakkuk 3:3).

And Zephaniah says: “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; proclaim it, daughter of Jerusalem; be glad and delight with all your heart. The Lord has taken away your wrongdoings; He has redeemed you from the hand of your enemies. The Lord will reign in your midst; you will no longer see evil” (Zephaniah 3:14-15).
And again: “Take courage, Zion; do not let your hands grow slack. The Lord God is in you; He is mighty to save you” (Zephaniah 3:16-17).
And Haggai says: “I am with you, says the Lord, and My Spirit stands over you” (Haggai 2:4-5).
And Zechariah says: “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, says the Lord” (Zechariah 2:10).
And again: “Behold, a man whose name is the Branch, and He will spring up from His place” (Zechariah 6:12).
And again: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: I will return to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and Jerusalem will be called the true city” (Zechariah 8:3).
translator_notes: The section opens partway through heading 94, which begins at the end of the chapter list in the previous section; the full heading in the body reads “That He will judge the world, and judgment will be given to Him.”

Headings 95-102 close the chapter list. The Greek numerals for 90 have fallen out of 95-99, so only the unit numerals survive, and heading 96 has lost its numeral entirely; the numbers follow the sequence.
Heading 100 has no verb in the Greek; “will come” is supplied from headings 93 and 97.
Headings 96, 101 and 102 echo Isaiah 34:4, Matthew 24:30 and Luke 1:33 but summarise rather than quote, so they carry no inline citation.

Epiphanius counts the Psalms by the Greek numbering (109, 71, 32, 106); the inline citations give the English numbers. “Psalm 106” restores a numeral missing from the printed text, which reads 100; the quotation is Greek Psalm 106:20 = Psalm 107:20.
In 1.2 and 3.1 “Wisdom” is the speaker of Proverbs 8, not the Book of Wisdom; 3.3 is Wisdom of Solomon 9:9, loosely quoted.
3.2: “breath of His mouth” renders πνεῦμα, which also means “Spirit”; the Fathers often read the verse of the Word and the Spirit together.
4.1: the edition reads “house of the tribe”; the Greek of Isaiah 42:7 has “prison”, which the sense requires. Epiphanius’s text also leaves out the middle of Isaiah 42:6.
4.2 follows the Gospel form of Malachi 3:1 (“before Your face”); the Greek of Malachi reads “before My face”. 4.3, introduced with “And again”, is Isaiah 61:1 (Luke 4:18).
5.2: the edition reads “his brothers”; the Greek of Deuteronomy and Acts 3:22 read “your brothers”. Kept as printed. The last clause follows Acts 3:23 rather than Deuteronomy 18:19.
5.4: the edition’s πεπρωκότα is a misprint for πεπτωκότα, “fallen parts”.
5.10 is compressed in the Greek; read as “Jonah will suffice to make the figure of the death plain” (compare Matthew 12:40).
5.11 joins Nahum 1:7 and Nahum 2:13 (Greek 2:14; the same words stand at 3:5).
5.12: in the Greek of Habakkuk 2:3 “the vision” is the subject; Epiphanius’s excerpt leaves it out, so the subject reads as “He”. 5.13 is Habakkuk 3:2.
Joel 3:16, 3:17 and 3:21 are Joel 4:16, 4:17 and 4:21 in the Greek; Zechariah 2:10 is 2:14 in the Greek (its opening, “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion”, matches Zechariah 9:9).
5.19: the Greek word means both “rising” and “shoot”; “Branch” follows the Hebrew sense and is kept the same at Jeremiah 23:5 in the next section.
baehrens: PG 41-43; Testimonia ex divinis et sacris scripturis (Khazarzar) u01 rem early

title: Prophets of His Coming
english: And Malachi says: “I am a great King, says the Lord Almighty, and My name will be renowned among the nations” (Malachi 1:14). “And suddenly He will come to His temple, says the Lord God, He whom you desire, and the Angel of the covenant, whom you seek. Behold, He comes, says the Lord” (Malachi 3:1). “He will rise for you who fear Him; His name is the Sun of Righteousness, and healing is in His wings” (Malachi 4:2).

Isaiah says: “In those last days the mountain of the Lord and the house of God will be plain to see on the top of the mountains; out of Zion will go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem” (Isaiah 2:2-3). “The Lord Himself will come for judgment with the elders of the people” (Isaiah 3:14).

And again: “On that day God will shine forth with glory upon the earth” (Isaiah 4:2). “A rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will come up from the root; and the Spirit of God will rest upon Him, the Spirit of wisdom, the Spirit of understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and godliness; and the Spirit of the fear of God will fill Him” (Isaiah 11:1-3).

And again: “You will see a King in glory” (Isaiah 33:17). “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make straight the paths of our God” (Isaiah 40:3). “Behold our God; behold, the Lord comes with strength” (Isaiah 40:9-10).
And again: “Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your Savior is coming, bringing His reward with Him” (Isaiah 62:11).
And again: “The hand of the Lord will be made known to those who fear Him” (Isaiah 66:14).
And again: “There will be the root of Jesse, He who rises to rule the nations; in Him the nations will hope” (Isaiah 11:10).
And again: “To You they will pray, because God is in You, and they will say: There is no God besides You; for You are God, and we did not know it” (Isaiah 45:14-15).
And Jeremiah says: “The Spirit before our face is Christ the Lord” (Lamentations 4:20).
And again: “Remember me, Lord, and visit me, and vindicate me against those who persecute me” (Jeremiah 15:15).

And again: “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, they are coming, and I will raise up for David a righteous Branch; and a King will reign and will act with understanding, and He will do judgment and righteousness on the earth. In His days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell trusting in Him. And this is His name, by which He will call Him: Josedek, and He is among the prophets” (Jeremiah 23:5-6).
And again: “They will know the Prophet whom the Lord sent to them in faithfulness” (Jeremiah 28:9).
And again: “Pray to Me, and I will hear you; you will seek and you will find Me, if you seek Me with all your heart, and I will appear to you” (Jeremiah 29:12-14).
And again: “The Lord is coming to His holy mountain of righteousness” (Jeremiah 31:23).
And Ezekiel says: “As for the likeness of their faces, all four had the face of a man, the face of a lion, the face of a calf and the face of an eagle” (Ezekiel 1:10).
And again: “I will remember My covenant with you in the days of your infancy, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant; and you will remember your way” (Ezekiel 16:60-61).
And again: “From My holy mountain, on a high mountain, says the Lord, there all the house of Israel will serve Me to the end” (Ezekiel 20:40).
And again: “Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will seek out My sheep and I will visit them, as a shepherd seeks his flock” (Ezekiel 34:11-12).
And again: “They will know that I am the Lord their God, when I appear to them among the nations” (Ezekiel 39:28).
And Balaam says: “A man will come forth from the seed of Israel, and He will rule over many nations” (Numbers 24:7).
And again: “A star will rise out of Jacob, and a man will rise up out of Israel, and He will crush the mighty of Moab” (Numbers 24:17).
And Daniel says: “Until Christ the Prince, seven weeks and sixty-two weeks” (Daniel 9:25).
And David says: “When the Lord turns back the captivity of His people, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad” (Psalm 14:7).

And again: “He Himself set His tent in the sun; and He, like a bridegroom coming out of His chamber, will rejoice like a giant to run the course. His going forth is from the end of heaven, and His circuit reaches to the end of heaven” (Psalm 19:4-6).
And again: “Make Your face shine upon Your servant” (Psalm 31:16).
And again: “He bowed the heavens and came down” (Psalm 18:9).
And again: “The God of gods will be seen in Zion” (Psalm 84:7).
And again: “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord; God is the Lord, and He has appeared to us” (Psalm 118:26-27).
And again: “The angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear Him, and will deliver them” (Psalm 34:7).
And again: “He will come down like rain upon a fleece” (Psalm 72:6).
And again: “The Lord is near to those who are broken in heart” (Psalm 34:18).
And again: “May He make His face shine upon…
translator_notes: This section continues chapter 5, “That He will come” (testimonies 5.21-5.52); 5.52 breaks off and ends at the start of the next section, where its citation (Psalm 67:1) is given.

5.21 joins Malachi 1:14, 3:1 and 4:2 (Greek 3:20). In 3:1 the edition reads “says the Lord God, He whom you desire”; the Greek of Malachi has “the Lord, whom you seek … whom you desire”. Kept as printed.
5.22: the edition reads “for anointing”, a slip for the near-identical Greek word “for judgment” (Isaiah 3:14); rendered “judgment”.
5.24 joins Isaiah 33:17 and 40:3, 9-10; the edition reads “our God” where the Greek of Isaiah 40:9 has “your God”. 5.28 is Isaiah 45:14-15 (“they will pray to You”).
5.29 is Lamentations 4:20, which Epiphanius, like other Fathers, gives under Jeremiah’s name; the edition reads “Christ the Lord” where the Greek of Lamentations has “the anointed of the Lord”.

5.31: “Josedek” is the Greek Old Testament’s form of the Hebrew name rendered “The Lord is our righteousness” in English Bibles (Jeremiah 23:6). The closing words “and He is among the prophets” answer to the heading “Concerning the prophets” that follows 23:6 directly in the Greek order (23:9); Epiphanius reads it as part of the oracle. The doubled “they are coming” is in the edition.

5.32 is Jeremiah 28:9 (Greek 35:9); 5.33 is Jeremiah 29:12-14 (Greek 36:12-14); 5.34 answers to Jeremiah 31:23 (Greek 38:23), where the Greek reads “Blessed be the Lord” for the edition’s “The Lord is coming”.
5.40 is Numbers 24:7 in the Greek; the edition reads “seed of Israel” where the Greek of Numbers has “his seed”.
“Angel” is capitalised where it is a title of Christ (the Angel of the covenant) and lower case in Psalm 34:7.
baehrens: PG 41-43; Testimonia ex divinis et sacris scripturis (Khazarzar) u01 rem mid

title: God Made Man, Born of a Virgin
english: …us, and may He have mercy on us” (Psalm 67:1).
And again: “All the peoples have seen the salvation of our God” (Psalm 98:3).
Solomon says: “Will God truly dwell with men?” (1 Kings 8:27; 2 Chronicles 6:18).
6. That He was seen, and that, being God, He became man.
Jeremiah says: “This is our God; no other will be reckoned beside Him. He found out every way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob His servant and to Israel, who was loved by Him” (Baruch 3:35-36).
And again: “He is a man, and who will know Him?” (Jeremiah 17:9).
And again: “After these things He was seen on earth and lived among men” (Baruch 3:37).
And David says: “Truth has sprung up from the earth” (Psalm 85:11).
And again: “And a man was born in her, and He Himself, the Most High, founded her” (Psalm 87:5).
Hosea says: “My flesh is from them. What shall I do with you, Ephraim? I will shield you, Israel, for I am God and not man” (Hosea 9:12; 11:8-9).
Isaiah says: “God is with us; know it, you nations, and be defeated” (Isaiah 8:8-9).
And again: “I became manifest to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me” (Isaiah 65:1).
And again: “To You they will pray, because God is in You, and there is no God besides You; for You are God, and we did not know it” (Isaiah 45:14-15).
7. That the Lord is of the seed of David.
David says in Psalm 88: “Once for all I have sworn by My holiness that I will not lie to David: his seed will remain for ever” (Psalm 89:35-36).
And again: “The Lord swore truth to David, and He will not go back on it: Of the fruit of your body I will set upon your throne” (Psalm 132:11).
And again: “I will establish his seed for ever and ever, and his throne as the days of heaven” (Psalm 89:29).
And Isaiah says: “I will set His kingdom upon the throne of David, to establish it and to uphold it in righteousness and judgment” (Isaiah 9:7).

And again Jeremiah: “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and a King will reign and will act with understanding, and He will do judgment and righteousness on the earth. In His days Israel will be saved, and Judah will dwell in Him” (Jeremiah 23:5-6).
8. That He comes from a virgin.

Isaiah, the great and glorious, is the first to cry aloud, saying: “Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a Son, and they will call His name Emmanuel,” which is translated “God with us” (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23).
9. That after He is born He will keep the mother who bore Him a virgin.

Ezekiel says: “The Lord said to me: Son of man, this gate will be shut; no one at all will pass through it but the Lord God alone; and He will enter and sit, for He is the Prince; and He will go out and shut the doors behind Him, and the gate will be shut for ever and ever” (Ezekiel 44:2-3).
10. That the womb is a gate.
Job says: “Why did you not shut the gates of my mother’s womb for me?” (Job 3:10).
11. That the virgin will give birth without pangs.
Isaiah cries aloud, saying: “Before she who was in labor gave birth, before the pain of her pangs came, she escaped and gave birth to a male” (Isaiah 66:7).
12. That He was anointed.
David says in Psalm 44: “Therefore God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of gladness above Your companions” (Psalm 45:7).
And Isaiah says: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me, because He has anointed Me” (Isaiah 61:1).
13. That on earth He is without a father and without intercourse.
Jeremiah says: “Woe is me, mother! As what kind of man have you borne me, a man at law and at odds with the whole earth?” (Jeremiah 15:10).

And David says in Psalm 21: “God, my God, attend to me” (Psalm 22:1). “For You are He who drew me out of the womb, my hope from my mother’s breasts; upon You I was cast from the womb; from my mother’s belly You are my God” (Psalm 22:9-10).
And Daniel: “He was watching until a stone was cut out without hands, and it struck the image” (Daniel 2:34).
And that He is a stone, Isaiah says: “Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and whoever believes in Him will not be put to shame” (Romans 9:33; Isaiah 8:14; 28:16).
And Zechariah says: “On the one stone there are seven eyes, looking upon all the earth” (Zechariah 3:9; 4:10).
14. That He is a child.
Isaiah bears witness, saying: “For a Child has been born to us, a Son has also been given to us, whose rule is upon His shoulder, and His name is called the Angel of Great Counsel” (Isaiah 9:6).
And again the same prophet says: “Before the Child knew how to call His father or His mother, He took the power of Damascus” (Isaiah 8:4).
And again: “A little child will write them down” (Isaiah 10:19).
15. That He will be born in Bethlehem.
Isaiah says: “He will dwell in a high place, upon a strong rock” (Isaiah 33:16).
16. That the Magi will worship Him.
David says in Psalm 71: “The kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts; the kings of the Arabians and of Sheba, gifts…” (Psalm 72:10).
translator_notes: The section opens with the end of 5.52 (Psalm 67:1, Greek 66:2), begun at the close of the previous section, and ends inside 16.1 (Psalm 72:10-11); the next section opens with “will bring them; and all the kings of the earth will worship Him”.

5.53: the edition’s wording is slightly garbled and ends with a question mark. It blends Psalm 98:3 (Greek 97:3, “all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God”) with Psalm 97:6 (“all the peoples”); rendered as a statement, as in the Psalm.
5.54 is 1 Kings 8:27 = 2 Chronicles 6:18, a question. Heading 6 has lost its numeral in the printed text.
6.1 and 6.3 are Baruch, which Epiphanius, like other Fathers, quotes under Jeremiah’s name. English Bibles number these verses Baruch 3:35-37 (Greek and Latin 3:36-38).
6.6 joins Hosea 9:12 and 11:8-9. 6.7 joins Isaiah 8:8 (“God is with us”) and 8:9. 6.9 repeats Isaiah 45:14-15 (as at 5.28) without “and they will say”; rendered as printed.

7.1: “that I will not lie to David” renders the Hebrew oath form (literally “if I lie to David…”), an emphatic denial. Psalm numbers 88, 44, 21 and 71 are Epiphanius’s Greek numbering; the citations give the English.
7.5 repeats Jeremiah 23:5-6 in a second form: here Israel is saved and Judah dwells “in Him”; kept as printed.
9.1: “no one at all” renders an emphatic double negative. The edition’s verb is read as “will sit”, as in the Greek of Ezekiel 44:3.

13a.1: Epiphanius cites Jeremiah 15:10 because the prophet speaks only of a mother. 13a.3: the edition reads “he was watching” where Theodotion’s Daniel 2:34 reads “You were watching”; kept as printed.
13b.1 follows the blend of Isaiah 28:16 and 8:14 found in Romans 9:33. 13b.2 joins Zechariah 3:9 and 4:10.

14.2 (Isaiah 8:4): the edition has the past tense, “He took”, where the Greek of Isaiah has the future; kept. 15.1 answers to Isaiah 33:16 (Greek: “in a high cave of strong rock”), which Justin also read of the cave at Bethlehem.
